name: Mastra framework and Mastra platform
summary: Mastra is an open-source TypeScript framework (`@mastra/core` and related `@mastra/*` packages) for agents, workflows, memory and tools, with a local Studio UI started by `mastra dev`. The Mastra platform, which replaces Mastra Cloud, is Mastra's hosted service with Observability, Studio and Server products.

tracing.what: Observability (the `Observability` class from `@mastra/observability`, set as `observability` on the Mastra instance) records a span for every agent run, workflow run, tool call and model call, with token counts and cost estimates. Exporters send spans to Studio (MastraStorageExporter), the Mastra platform (MastraPlatformExporter) or third-party tools such as Langfuse, Braintrust and Arize.

portability.note: Spans and exporters use Mastra's own open-source interface. The OtelExporter (`@mastra/otel-exporter`) sends traces and logs to any OTLP endpoint (http/json, http/protobuf or grpc) using the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, and an OtelBridge links Mastra spans to existing OpenTelemetry context.

evaluations.what: Evals use scorers (prebuilt ones in `@mastra/evals`, custom ones made with `createScorer`) that score agent and workflow outputs live on sampled traffic through the `scorers` option, or in batches with `runEvals`; datasets and experiments run an agent or workflow against stored test cases. Scores are saved to the `mastra_scorers` table in the configured storage and shown in Studio.

portability.note: Scorers and score records use Mastra's own interface and are stored in the developer's own database through the open-source framework. The docs show no open standard format for eval data.

prompt-management.what: Editor (`MastraEditor` from `@mastra/editor`, set as `editor` on the Mastra instance) stores agent instructions and reusable prompt blocks with draft and published versions, edited in Studio; agents that reference a prompt block use its active published version at run time.

portability.note: Versions use Mastra's own format, kept in the developer's configured storage by default or, with `source: 'code'`, as JSON override files in the repository. No open standard for prompts is involved.

evidence.note: Override files written when the Editor uses source: 'code'.

keys-and-secrets.what: Mastra platform environments store variables as write-only encrypted secrets or readable config values, set in the dashboard or with `mastra env vars set`, and deliver them to the service at boot; the framework reads model provider keys from environment variables such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Connect (Public Beta) on the Mastra platform holds OAuth or API-key connections to services such as GitHub and Slack, adding credentials on the server for tool calls or returning them through `credential()`.

portability.note: Agent code reads plain environment variables, which any host can supply. The platform's secret storage, the `mastra env vars` commands and Connect are Mastra's own hosted features.

memory-and-state.what: Memory (`@mastra/memory`) gives agents message history, working memory, semantic recall and observational memory, scoped by `thread` and `resource` ids, and workflow snapshots let suspended runs resume. State is kept in a storage adapter set on the Mastra instance, such as LibSQLStore (`@mastra/libsql`) or PostgresStore (`@mastra/pg`).

portability.note: Threads, messages, working memory and snapshots use Mastra's own data format, stored in the developer's own database through open-source adapters for libSQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB and others. No open standard for agent memory is involved.

human-approval.what: Workflow steps pause with `suspend()` and continue with `run.resume()`, and agent tool calls pause for approval through `requireApproval` on `createTool()` or `requireToolApproval` per request, answered with `approveToolCall()` or `declineToolCall()`. Paused runs survive restarts only when persistent storage is configured.

portability.note: This is Mastra's own API in the open-source framework, with snapshots kept in the developer's configured storage. No open standard is involved.

deployment.what: `mastra build` produces a standalone Hono-based server in `.mastra/output` that runs on Node.js, Bun or Deno, with optional deployers for Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare. `mastra deploy` releases the app to the Mastra platform, which replaces Mastra Cloud with separate Studio and Server products and per-environment URLs and variables.

portability.note: The built server comes from the open-source framework and runs on any host that supports Node.js, Bun or Deno. The Mastra platform and `mastra deploy` are Mastra's hosted service, and the provider deployers target each provider's own format.

sandboxes.what: A Workspace (`Workspace` from `@mastra/core/workspace`) gives an agent a sandbox for running commands and code plus a filesystem, using LocalSandbox or provider packages for services such as E2B, Daytona, Modal and Vercel; the Mastra platform provisions managed Workspaces through `@mastra/platform-workspace`. The docs state that LocalSandbox runs commands on the host and is not isolated by default.

portability.note: The Workspace interface is Mastra's own and open source. Isolation comes from the chosen provider, several of which are third-party services, and the managed Workspaces are a Mastra platform service.

tool-connections.what: `@mastra/mcp` provides MCPClient, which connects agents to MCP servers over stdio or Streamable HTTP (with `authenticate()` for OAuth-protected servers), and MCPServer, which exposes a Mastra app's agents, tools and workflows as an MCP server. The MCP events support (SEP-3415, a draft extension) is labeled experimental.

portability.note: Tools reached through MCPClient and MCPServer use the open protocol (the docs name the 2026-07-28 revision). Tools defined with `createTool()` use Mastra's own interface but can be exposed to other clients through MCPServer.

agent-to-agent.what: Mastra serves each registered agent as an A2A endpoint with an agent card (`/api/.well-known/<agentId>/agent-card.json`) and an execution URL (`/api/a2a/<agentId>`), supporting A2A 0.3.0 and 1.0, and `A2AAgent` from `@mastra/core/a2a` or `getA2A()` in `@mastra/client-js` call remote A2A agents. The docs note that A2A task records and push notification configs are kept in memory and lost on restart.

portability.note: Both serving and calling follow the A2A protocol over JSON-RPC with Server-Sent Events streaming, and agent cards can be signed with ES256.

evidence.note: Key under server.a2a on the Mastra instance.

identity-and-access.what: Auth providers set on `server.auth` protect the Mastra API and Studio: built-in Simple Auth and JSON Web Token (`MastraJwtAuth` in `@mastra/auth`) plus provider packages for Auth0, Better Auth, Clerk, Firebase, Google, Neon, Okta, Supabase and WorkOS, with role-based access control and fine-grained authorization. Authentication is optional, and without it all routes and Studio are public.

portability.note: The provider interface is Mastra's own, while providers such as Okta use an OAuth 2.0 / OIDC sign-in flow and verify Bearer JWTs against the identity provider's JWKS. Fine-grained authorization (`@mastra/core/auth/ee`) requires a Mastra Enterprise Edition license in production.

packaging.what: Mastra agents load skills that follow the Agent Skills specification (a folder with a `SKILL.md` carrying `name` and `description`), through a Workspace `skills` option, the agent's `skills` config or `createSkill()`; the docs do not mention Agent Plugins. Mastra's own layout puts the Mastra instance in `src/mastra/index.ts`, with file-based agents in `src/mastra/agents/<name>/` (`config.ts`, `instructions.md`, `skills/`).

portability.note: Skills use the open Agent Skills format and can be read by other tools that support it. The project layout, the Mastra instance file and file-based agent folders are Mastra's own conventions, and no Agent Plugins `plugin.json` support is documented.
